pitfalls: 粉色 and 粉红色 mean the same; 粉色 is shorter and more frequent in speech.
subtleties: ‘What colour is it?’ = 是什么颜色的？ — 颜色 yánsè is ‘colour’.
The colour as a noun: before a noun it takes 的 (白色的车), as a predicate 是…的 (车是白色的), and alone it is the colour itself (我喜欢白色).

profile.feeling: Purple — lavender, plums, imperial grandeur.

etymology.text: 紫 ‘purple’ (phonetic 此 + semantic 糸 ‘silk’) + 色 ‘colour’.

funFacts: The Forbidden City is 紫禁城 ‘the Purple Forbidden City’ — purple after the Pole Star, home of the heavenly emperor.
pitfalls: A red onion is 紫洋葱 ‘purple onion’, and 紫菜 is seaweed (nori), not a purple vegetable.
subtleties: ‘What colour is it?’ = 是什么颜色的？ — 颜色 yánsè is ‘colour’.
The colour as a noun: before a noun it takes 的 (白色的车), as a predicate 是…的 (车是白色的), and alone it is the colour itself (我喜欢白色).

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound (traditional 淺): semantic 氵 ‘water’ + phonetic 戔 — first ‘shallow’.

funFacts: Chinese uses the words for water depth for colours: 浅 ‘shallow’ = light, 深 ‘deep’ = dark.
pitfalls: ‘Light’ has three Chinese words: a light colour 浅, light in weight 轻 qīng, bright with light 亮 liàng.
subtleties: 浅 joins the colour word directly: 浅蓝色, 浅绿色 (no 的).

etymology.text: Phono-semantic compound: semantic 氵 ‘water’ + phonetic — first ‘deep’ (of water).

funFacts: 深 and 浅 are a water pair — deep and shallow — used for strong and pale colours.
pitfalls: A dark ROOM is 暗 or 黑 (房间很暗), not 深: 深 is for colours, water and feelings.
subtleties: 深 joins the colour word directly: 深蓝色, 深绿色 (no 的).

senses.def: more, even more (before an adjective or a verb of liking)
(read gēng) to change, replace (更新 ‘to update’)

examples.tr: Today is even colder than yesterday.

phrases.text: 欲穷千里目，更上一层楼
phrases.tr: to see a thousand li further, climb one more storey
phrases.meaning: to see further, rise higher (said of striving for more)
phrases.source: Wang Zhihuan, 登鹳雀楼 (Tang dynasty)

synonyms.nuance: hái: even (more) — in comparisons, with surprise: 他比我还高 ‘he is even taller than me’
gèngjiā: even more (written)

etymology.text: Originally an ideogram of two chariots (丙); later a hand with a whip 攴 was added and one 丙 dropped (Shuowen 㪅).

funFacts: 更上一层楼 ‘climb one more storey’ comes from a famous Tang poem and is used for any further progress.
pitfalls: 更 gèng ‘more’ vs 更 gēng ‘to change’ (更新 ‘update’) — same character, two readings.
Never 很 with 更: *更很好 → 更好.
subtleties: 更 compares even without 比: 我觉得这个更好 ‘I think this one is better’.
更 can come after a 比-phrase: 他比我更高 ‘he is (even) taller than me’.

examples.py: Zhè shì zuì hǎo de fànguǎn.

synonyms.nuance: zuìwéi: most (written, before two-syllable adjectives: 最为重要)

etymology.text: Originally 㝡: semantic 宀 ‘roof’ + phonetic 取 ‘to gather’; marks were added to set apart the sense ‘the most’, and the top later became 曰 in simplified writing.

funFacts: 最后 ‘finally, the last’ is ‘most behind’.
pitfalls: No 很 with 最: *最很高 → 最高.
最好 + verb means ‘you had better’: 你最好早点走 ‘you’d better leave early’.
subtleties: 最 + adjective + 的 = ‘the …-est (one)’: 最大的 ‘the biggest’; the group comes first: 我们家我爸爸最高.

synonyms.nuance: gēn … bǐ: compared with … (跟去年比 ‘compared with last year’)

etymology.text: Explained as two 匕 side by side (phono-semantic, Chu Wan-li) or as an ideogram ‘to juxtapose’ (Shuowen); graphically like 从 and 北 but unrelated.

funFacts: 比 looks like two people standing side by side — the picture of comparing.
pitfalls: After 比 + noun the adjective stands alone: *他比我很高 → 他比我高 (or 他比我高多了 ‘much taller’).
The negation is 没有, not 不比: 他没有我高 ‘he isn’t as tall as me’; 他不比我高 means ‘he’s no taller than me’ (we’re about the same).
subtleties: The difference comes after the adjective: 他比我大两岁 ‘he is two years older than me’, 贵一点 ‘a bit more expensive’.

etymology.text: 一 ‘one’ + 样 ‘kind, manner, shape’: ‘of one kind’.
etymology.src: morphemes: 一 + 样 (Wiktionary (kaikki.org) character entries)

funFacts: 一模一样 ‘one mould, one shape’ — like two prints from the same mould.
pitfalls: No 很 in an equal comparison: *我跟他一样很高 → 我跟他一样高.
一 is read yí here (before the 4th tone of 样).
subtleties: 不一样 ‘not the same’ is the everyday word for ‘different’: 我们不一样.
